script: Sent Scammer Dirty Diapers and More. I used to own a commercial embroidery business. One day the phone rang. A guy on the other end asked for a specific brand of garments we got from our wholesale supplier. He wanted an order worth about $2,000, but no decoration. He said he'd pay the next day. A FedEx envelope hit my doorstep overnight. Inside was a business check made out to my company. I called the company on the check and spoke with their CFO. He was a mess, but the account was legit. The scammer pinged me right after, "Did you get the check?" He promised a courier would pick up the boxes the next day. So I filled four empty boxes with garbage from home—dirty diapers, used cat litter, my neighbor's trash, and some shop junk. I taped them tight and waited. A FedEx truck rolled up. I asked for the pickup details. They handed me a tracking number. I checked the tracker the next day. The boxes were on an overnight flight to Kenya. I am sure someone's credit card paid a crazy shipping charge. I never heard from that guy again. I was hoping he'd get mad about the garbage, but instead I just got a silent trip to Africa. (I know, right?)
